purpose: Source-based acceptance checklist, written independently of generated graphs. Evaluation data only; never consumed by the extraction, background, graph review or quiz pipelines.

ai_three_paragraphs.txt.claim: A supervised classifier learns an input-to-label mapping using labeled training examples.
During training an optimization algorithm adjusts model parameters to reduce the loss function.
The loss function measures disagreement between model predictions and training labels.
The loss function provides a signal for parameter updates.
Validation examples are separate from the training set.
Developers use validation results to select model settings before evaluating the chosen model on a held-out test set.
Good training performance alone does not guarantee good performance on unseen examples from the intended application. Unseen does not necessarily mean out of distribution.
Regularization can reduce overfitting by limiting fitting of incidental training-data details.
After training, quantization represents model parameters with fewer bits.
Quantization can reduce the memory needed to store model parameters.
Lower numerical precision can reduce prediction accuracy; a decrease is not guaranteed.
The quantized model should be evaluated again because prediction accuracy may decrease.

neuron_three_paragraphs.txt.claim: A typical neuron has a cell body.
A typical neuron has an axon.
The cell body contains the nucleus.
Dendrites receive many signals arriving from other neurons.
The axon conducts action potentials toward its terminals.
Axonal conduction of action potentials allows the neuron to communicate with other cells.
An action potential involves a rapid change in voltage across the neuronal membrane.
Opening voltage-gated sodium channels allows sodium ions to enter during depolarization.
Subsequent opening of voltage-gated potassium channels allows potassium ions to leave, contributing to repolarization.
Myelin can increase action-potential conduction speed along an axon.
At a chemical synapse, an arriving action potential opens calcium channels in the presynaptic terminal.
Calcium entry triggers neurotransmitter release from synaptic vesicles into the synaptic cleft.
The neurotransmitter binds receptors on the postsynaptic cell.
Depending on the receptor, neurotransmitter binding can increase or decrease the likelihood of a postsynaptic action potential.
